chunks: Like the chest/bosom of a bird in the deep sea.

key_terms.جُؤْجُؤ: The chest or bosom of a bird
key_terms.لُجَّة: The deep part of the sea; a vast expanse of water

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the metaphor 'like the bosom of a bird in the deep sea' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi employs this vivid metaphor in the context of condemning the Basrans to illustrate their spiritual disorientation and insignificance amidst the vastness of divine decree. The image of a bird's chest bobbing in the deep sea underscores their lack of firm grounding in truth, serving as a critique of their political and moral vacillation during the early Islamic period.
